public_rationale: The accessible [report](https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/openai-lifts-planned-compute-spending-144917731.html) places approximately $750 billion of projected spending through 2030. That does not match the next three years from September 2026. The mismatch prevents support, but a longer-period total alone does not establish a contradictory three-year total. This is an observation about an existing projection, so it is not a forecast awaiting its deadline.
limitations: The original linked report could not be read with read_page.
The accessible evidence is secondary reporting of a private projection.
A total through 2030 cannot be allocated to shorter periods without a spending schedule.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI projects $750 billion or more in compute spending over three years, so Altman's openness to a pause is worrying.

statement.excerpt: This is a very, very worrying thing for Altman to say given that OpenAI has projected to spend $750 billion or more in the next three years across compute contracts with Microsoft, Google, Amazon, CoreWeave, Cerebras and other providers.
statement.document_title: AI Is Already In Dangerous Hands

from_speaker: Microsoft, Google, Amazon, CoreWeave, Cerebras and other providers
our_interpretation: Assess the existence and content of OpenAI's standing projection, not whether future spending ultimately occurs.
The statement that Altman's position is worrying is evaluative and is not scored.
Read the next three years as the rolling period from September 14, 2026 through September 14, 2029. Calendar-year interpretations remain possible.
For this ongoing projection, use a snapshot as of the post date rather than an earnings quarter. The spending period is recorded separately in metric_scope.
Use estimate as the accounting basis because the post links its amount to press reporting of projections.
Projected cumulative spending is neither an annualized run rate nor already realized spending.
criteria.support_condition: A projection current at publication assigns at least USD 750 billion of OpenAI compute spending to the specified three-year period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comprehensive projection current at publication assigns less than USD 750 billion to the same company, compute-spending scope, and three-year period.

evidence.explanation: The reported projection matches the approximate amount but runs through 2030. It cannot establish or refute spending within the shorter three-year window, and the underlying projection document was unavailable.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A projection current at publication with a dated compute-spending schedule covering September 2026 through September 2029, or clarification of the intended three calendar years and a matching schedule.
